Gene Set Variation Analysis (GSVA)

rna_gsva.Rd

Estimates pathway activity scores for individual samples using gene expression data and predefined gene sets. Gene sets can be obtained from a previous rna_gsea() analysis, MSigDB collections, or user-supplied pathways.

Unlike GSEA, which evaluates pathway enrichment between experimental conditions using a ranked gene list, GSVA-based methods estimate pathway-level variation across individual samples, allowing downstream comparisons and longitudinal analyses.

Usage

rna_gsva(
  project,
  source = c("gsea", "msigdb", "custom"),
  pathways = NULL,
  pathway_scope = c("top", "significant", "all"),
  geneset_collection = "H",
  geneset_subcollection = NULL,
  method = c("gsva", "ssgsea", "zscore", "plage"),
  kcdf = "Gaussian",
  min_size = 10,
  max_size = 500,
  save = TRUE
)

Arguments

project

An rna_project object containing normalized gene expression data.

source

Character specifying the source of gene sets: "gsea" to reuse pathways from a previous GSEA analysis, "msigdb" to retrieve gene sets from MSigDB, or "custom" to use user-supplied pathways.

pathways

Optional named list of gene sets, required when source = "custom". Each element should contain gene identifiers corresponding to the expression matrix.

pathway_scope

Character specifying which pathways to retrieve from a previous GSEA result: "top", "significant", or "all". Only applicable when source = "gsea".

geneset_collection

Character specifying the MSigDB collection when source = "msigdb" (e.g., "H", "C2", "C5").

geneset_subcollection

Optional character specifying an MSigDB subcollection (e.g., "CP:REACTOME", "GO:BP").

method

Character specifying the pathway scoring method: "gsva", "ssgsea", "zscore", or "plage".

kcdf

Character specifying the kernel distribution used by GSVA to estimate expression distributions.

min_size

Integer specifying the minimum number of genes required for a gene set to be included in the analysis.

max_size

Integer specifying the maximum number of genes allowed in a gene set.

save

Logical. If TRUE, stores the GSVA result in the rna_project object.

gsea

Optional object of class gsea_result, required when source = "gsea".

Value

An object of class gsva_result containing the pathway activity scores and associated analysis information.

Gene set sources

Gene sets can be obtained from three different sources:

  • GSEA: reuses pathways from a previous rna_gsea() analysis. The pathway_scope argument determines whether the top-ranked, statistically significant, or all available pathways are considered.

    \item \strong{MSigDB:} retrieves gene sets directly from Molecular
  Signatures Database collections, allowing pathway activity estimation
  independently of a previous GSEA analysis.

\item \strong{Custom:} accepts user-defined gene sets, allowing the
  evaluation of specific biological signatures or experimental gene
  lists.

Scoring methods

Four methods are available for estimating pathway activity:

  • GSVA: estimates variation in pathway activity across samples using a non-parametric approach based on expression distributions.

    \item \strong{ssGSEA:} calculates enrichment scores for each gene set
  within individual samples based on gene expression rankings.

\item \strong{z-score:} combines standardized expression values of genes
  within each gene set to estimate pathway-level scores.

\item \strong{PLAGE:} uses singular value decomposition (SVD) to derive
  pathway activity scores from the expression profiles of genes within
  each set.

These methods differ in their scoring assumptions and numerical properties. Scores obtained using different methods should not be assumed to be directly comparable.

Interpretation

The resulting scores represent relative pathway-level expression patterns across samples and can be used in downstream analyses, including differential comparisons, clustering, correlation analysis, and longitudinal modeling.

Higher scores generally indicate stronger representation of the corresponding gene expression signature, but do not necessarily demonstrate increased biochemical activity or functional activation of the pathway. For PLAGE, score direction is arbitrary and should be interpreted with respect to the underlying expression patterns.

Results depend on the selected gene sets, gene identifier compatibility, expression data, and scoring method. Gene sets containing too few or too many genes after matching to the expression matrix are excluded according to min_size and max_size.

Pipeline context

GSVA is typically performed after expression normalization and before downstream statistical analyses. Unlike GSEA, it does not require a previous differential expression comparison and can therefore be used to investigate pathway-level variation across all samples in a project.
